items.text: The UK’s first drone delivery service that can be conducted permanent ly has been launched in Orkney to provide locals with their mail. Orkey’s a group of islands, and it’s introduced the first mail delivery in the country. The Orkney I-Port initiative, in collaboration with Royal Mail and drone company Skyports, aims to transport letters and packages between islands. The program involves cooperation with the local council’s harbor authority and Loganair Airline. Initially lasting three months, the drone service may become permanent due to Orkney’s unique landscape and close island proximity . This innovation is expected to enhance delivery speed and reliability to remote areas like Graemsay and Hoy, often affected by weather and geography disruptions. The fully electric drones, operated by Skyports, will carry items between islands using the Speedbird Aero DLV-2 drone, capable of transporting up to 6 kilograms. This effort is funded by the Department for Transport’s Freight Innovation Fund. Difficult words: permanent (lasting for a long time or forever), proximity (closeness), enhance (to increase or improve the quality or extent of something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Orkney, a UK island group, now employs drones to deliver mail. Royal Mail and Skyports launched Orkney I-Port, and they want to move letters and parcels between islands. This initiative uses electric drones for delivery. At first, it will run for three months and it will possibly continue. Orkney has a special landscape and close islands. Drones will improve service and delivery time to Graemsay and Hoy, which often have problems because of bad weather and geography. The drones operate with the Speedbird Aero DLV-2 drone and they can carry up to 6 kilograms. Royal Mail hopes that the project will help reduce carbon emissions. Difficult words: parcel (a box which people send by post), initiative (a new plan or process to achieve something or solve a problem), landscape (an area of land). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Orkney is a group of islands. Orkney belongs to the UK. The islands now use drones for mail. Royal Mail and Skyports make Orkney I-Port. Drones move letters and parcels between islands. The drones use batteries. They help make the air cleaner. Drones will deliver mail for three months. If it works well, they will continue after this time. There is a strong wind in Orkneys. It is not easy to move between the islands. It takes cars and ships a long time to travel there. Drones solve these problems. They can carry up to 6 kilograms. Transport’s Fund pays the project . Difficult words: drone (a flying robot), parcel (a box which people send by post), project (a piece of work). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A video shows a social experiment created to see how passers-by react to breastfeeding in public spaces. Two actors came on a train in England to initiate the experiment. One of the actors, a woman, started breastfeeding on the train which was met with criticism from a man sitting next to one seat from her. He, too, was an actor. He said that he felt ‘a bit uncomfortable about’ the breastfeeding and would prefer that the woman not do it in front of him. The actress did not care about his request, and their exchange started escalating . After the seat between the two vacated , a passenger who witnessed the confrontation took the seat and told the man that he was acting quite aggressively. Not long after, a camera man came out and informed everyone of the experiment. Difficult words: passer-by (a person who happens to be somewhere), initiate (start), next to one seat (there was one seat between them), exchange (a short conversation or argument), escalate (become more intense), vacate (become empty). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People created a social experiment to see how others really react to breastfeeding in public spaces. Part of the experiment showed a situation on the tube in London. An actress started breastfeeding on the train and a man, also an actor, was not happy about it. He told her that she was making him feel uncomfortable, and he asked her to stop. The man became increasingly louder and one of the passengers stepped in . He took a seat between the man and the woman to show his support for the mother. A moment afterwards, a person with a camera entered the carriage and told everyone about the experiment. Difficult words: increasingly (more and more), step in (to get involved in a situation), carriage (one part of the train). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This happens in London. A woman is on a train. She is a mother. She has her baby with her. She breastfeeds her baby. A man sees this. He does not like it. He starts to talk to the woman. He tells her to stop. He is loud and unpleasant . Other people see this situation. One man wants to help the woman. He sits between the other man and the woman. Soon, a person with a camera comes. The person tells everyone that the situation is an experiment . Difficult words: breastfeed (when a woman gives a baby milk from her breast), unpleasant (not nice), experiment (a situation which can give you information about something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

South Africa secured their first-ever Women’s World Cup win with a thrilling 3-2 victory over Italy, advancing to the last 16 of the tournament. Thembi Kgatlana scored the winning goal in stoppage time , crushing Italy’s hopes of progressing with just a draw. Earlier, Italy had taken the lead through a penalty, but an own goal helped South Africa level the score. In the second half, South Africa went ahead, only for Italy to equalize from a corner. In the end, Kgatlana’s late heroics sealed the win for South Africa. Coach Desiree Ellis praised her team’s fighting spirit and historic achievement. Now, South Africa is set to face the Netherlands in the next round. Difficult words: stoppage time (the period that is added to the end of the game because play was stopped during the game), equalize (to level the score in a match by scoring a goal), heroics (unusual actions or achievements). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

South Africa celebrated their first Women’s World Cup win. The team beat Italy 3-2 and secured a spot in the last 16. The match was intense, and Thembi Kgatlana’s last-minute goal ensured their victory. Italy had hoped for a draw to continue in the cup, but it was not meant to be. The Italians took the lead with a penalty, but South Africa equalized due to an own goal. Later, South Africa went ahead, and Italy responded with another goal from a corner. In the end, Kgatlana’s goal secured the win for South Africa. Coach Desiree Ellis praised her team’s fighting spirit and historic achievement. Next, South Africa will face the Netherlands in Sydney on Sunday. Difficult words: ensure (to make certain that something will happen), draw (when a game ends with the score even), equalize (to level the score in a match). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

South Africa wins their first Women’s World Cup match. They play against Italy. The score is 3-2. Thembi Kgatlana scores the winning goal in the last moments of the game. This victory means that South Africa will move to the next round of the tournament. Italy needs only a draw to continue in the tournament. But it does not happen. They score the first goal from a penalty. Then, South Africa gets a point with an own goal. Later, South Africa is leading. Italy scores again from a corner. But Kgatlana’s goal ensures South Africa’s victory. Coach Desiree Ellis says that the team fights hard. It is an important moment in South Africa’s history. Difficult words: victory (the moment when someone wins), draw (when two teams or players score the same number of points in a game or match), ensure (to make sure that something will happen). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

As part of campaign for Airbnb , film maker Leon Stuparich travelled 322 kilometres from London to Glastonbury on foot, completely relying on the kindness of strangers. He said that he wanted to test whether kindness and love was enough to survive in 21st century Britain. His group’s experience was that if you meet somebody with a smile and you take time to understand that person’s story as well, then people will come forward and they will naturally be kind. They automatically turn around and say, ‘Well, what can we do for you? What can we offer?’ People made his group tea, brought the people leftover rice and one time, even gave them keys to their apartment. Stuparich said that it was probably the most drastic night when they did not know where they were going to stay and one in the group was really sick. It was that night that they were screening the film ‘Road to Peace’ in an arts centre that someone said, ‘Here are the keys. Let yourself come and go as you please!’ Difficult words: Airbnb (a website that helps people find homes to rent for vacations), rely (depend upon), turn around (change how you feel suddenly), drastic (extreme), screen (to show a film). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A man decided to test lessons which he learned from the Dalai Lama and he went on a pilgrimage . He and others went on a 322-kilometre journey from London to Glastonbury. The people had no money – they wanted to see if it was possible to live through kindness . It seems, that in 21st century Britain, it is. The man talked about their experience – he said that when you smile at people, take time to understand their story, then they will come forward and are naturally kind. One woman gave them rice and a man brought them all tea. And one time, a person even gave them the keys to his flat! Difficult words: pilgrimage (a journey, usually to a special place), kindness (kind behaviour or nice behaviour), experience (something that happens to you). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A man learns lessons from the Dalai Lama. He wants to test these lessons. Other people and he go on a journey . They go from London to Glastonbury. The people have no money. They want to see if people will be kind to them. People are kind to them. The man talks about his journey. One woman gives them rice. A man makes all of them tea. One person even gives them the keys to his home! Difficult words: journey (a trip), will (this means “in the future”), kind (nice). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

German discount supermarket Penny is asking shoppers to pay extra for certain groceries to cover their true cost and raise awareness of the environmental impact of food production. Germans currently pay only 11.1% of their household budget for food, enjoying some of Europe’s cheapest groceries. However, this cheap food production comes at a high environmental price, with German agriculture responsible for a significant portion of greenhouse emissions. During the true cost campaign, customers will be charged prices that include climate, health, soil, and water costs for selected products, and any extra income will be donated to sustainable farming projects. The initiative aims to make consumers consider the environmental consequences of their purchases. Difficult words: awareness (when people know that something exists), initiative (an act or strategy intended to resolve a difficulty or improve a situation). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Discount supermarket Penny in Germany asked customers to pay more money for some food to make them aware of the true cost of food production. Germans paid only 11.1% of their household budget for food, less than people in the EU usually pay. But cheap food often leads to high environmental costs. Penny charged customers for selected products, and the company considered climate, health, soil, and water costs. The extra money which Penny makes will go to sustainable farming projects. The supermarket expected lower sales because of inflation and higher prices. Experts will study the impact of Penny’s campaign on consumers. Difficult words: household budget (how much money a family has for spending), sustainable (something what can last for a long time without a negative impact), inflation (the price of money). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Penny is a supermarket. It sells cheap food. Penny in Germany wants people to pay more money for food. People must understand the true cost of food. Cheap food has a bad impact on the natural world. Germans spend only 11.1% of their money on food. It is less than people in the EU usually pay. Penny will charge more money for some products. The extra money will go to help farming. Penny expects fewer sales because of higher prices and inflation. The government wants to reduce the impact of farming on the natural world. Experts will study how people react to Penny’s new prices. Difficult words: charge (to ask for a price), sale (when someone sells something to people), reduce (to make something smaller or less important). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A cost- conscious teen wanted to travel from Sheffield in northern England to Essex, which was around 300 kilometres from his location. He wanted to travel home by train but was ‘absolutely astonished at the price’. He then found out that it was actually cheaper to get a bus and a train from Sheffield to East Midlands Airport, get a flight to Berlin, Germany, fly from Berlin to Stansted, London, and then get a bus back home. All those extra 1,600 kilometres saved Brian a few pennies, but took him 13 hours from door-to-door . However, the adventurous teenager made his point as well as enjoyed the experience. He said that he would definitely do it again. Difficult words: conscious (concerned – worried about), astonished (greatly surprised), door-to-door (from the exact place that you left to the exact place that you wanted to get to). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A British teen wanted to get from the central area of England to the south, but the price of a one-way train ticket shocked him. He decided to take action and found out that it was cheaper to take a plane to Berlin first and then fly to his final destination from there. He travelled an extra 1,600 kilometres to save a little money. The journey took him 13 hours, but he said that it was a great experience . Difficult words: decide (to think about something and choose to do something), destination (a place where you want to go), experience (something which happens to you). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A teen is in central England. He wants to travel to the south of England. He wants to take the train, but it is very expensive. He looks for a cheaper way. He takes a plane to Berlin. From there, he flies back to England. He travels an extra 1,600 kilometres. He arrives at his destination in 13 hours. However, it is still cheaper than the train! Difficult words: teen (a teenager, a person between the age of 13 and 19), arrive (to come to a place), destination (the place where you want to go). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An owner of a tiny hedgehog filmed the animal cleaning herself, and now Nuala is a sensation on the Internet. The owner is happy about the attention, but she does not want people to rush out to get hedgehogs of their own. Hedgehogs are more high-maintenance than other small animals like hamsters or guinea pigs, as they need more care and attention. If you want one of these animals, make sure to understand how you will be caring for it! Difficult words: sensation (a hit), rush out (go quickly), high-maintenance (when something needs a lot of attention). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A cute female hedgehog was filmed while she was cleaning herself. The footage was uploaded on the internet and it has become very popular. The animal’s owner is happy that people like her hedgehog, but she is also worried. She is worried that people will soon want to have hedgehogs like hers as their pets. Hedgehogs are not like hamsters or guinea pigs. Hedgehogs need more care and not everyone can give it to them. Difficult words: female (connected with animals that produce eggs, not male), footage (film), pet (animal at home). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A woman has a beautiful hedgehog . The woman films it. The video is very nice. It is on the internet. A lot of people like this video. It is very popular. People like the animal, too. Maybe they want to have one. Hedgehogs need a lot of care . Not all people can give this care. They must read on how to take care before they buy a hedgehog. Difficult words: hedgehog (small animal with sharp things on its back), care (help). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The car carrier ship Fremantle Highway caught fire off the northernmost Dutch coast, carrying almost 500 electric vehicles along with other cars. The fire resulted in the death of an Indian crew member, and seven others were injured while trying to escape. Ship charter company K Line confirmed the presence of 498 battery electric vehicles among the 3,783 vehicles on board. BMW and Mercedes-Benz stated they also had cars on the ship. The cause of the fire is unknown, but there are concerns about extinguishing it due to the higher heat and longer duration of lithium-ion battery fires. Salvagers have managed to board the ship to secure tow lines , and authorities are investigating the incident. Difficult words: duration (the time during which something continues), salvager (rescuer), tow line (a rope or cable used for towing a vehicle or ship). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A ship carrying more than 3,700 cars, caught fire near the Dutch coast. The ship has about 500 electric vehicles on board, including BMW and Mercedes-Benz. The fire caused the death of one crew member, and seven others jumped into the water to save themselves. Ship charter company K Line revealed that they had 498 electric cars on the ship. The cause of the fire is not known yet, but lithium-ion battery fires can be difficult to put out because they burn hotter and last longer than gasoline fires. Rescuers managed to get on board to secure stronger tow lines . Authorities are investigating the incident. Difficult words: reveal (to say something in public), put out (to stop a fire), tow line (a rope or cable which people use to move a vehicle or ship). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A big ship carries cars on the sea. The ship catches fire. There are about 3,700 cars onboard . About 500 electric cars are among them. BMW and Mercedes-Benz confirm that their cars are onboard, too. It is not clear yet why the fire starts. But electric cars have different batteries. They burn hotter and longer. It is difficult to stop the fire. One person dies in the fire. Seven men are safe. They jump into the water. Authorities try to find out why the fire starts. The ship is still burning. The fire is not so strong. Rescuers can go on the ship and make it safe. Difficult words: onboard (on a ship or plane), confirm (to say that something is true). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Angie Xue fulfilled her dream of traveling to Japan and Korea by booking a 600-dollar round-trip flight from California. Before her trip, she arranged a personal color analysis appointment in Seoul after discovering it through viral videos. Personal color analysis helps individuals find flatterin g colors for clothing, makeup, and accessories based on their complexions and skin tones. The procedure involves draping fabric swatches to identify colors that enhance the person’s appearance. The trend fueled by TikTok is gaining popularity among Gen Z, leading many to travel to Seoul for the service. However, getting an appointment can be challenging. The boom in color analysis tourism has led the Korea Tourism Organization to promote international visits, resulting in increased retail spending. The trend also creates job opportunities, with a demand for English-speaking practitioners in the field. Difficult words: flattering (enhancing someone’s appearance), complexion (the natural color and texture of a person’s skin), swatch (a small sample of fabric intended to demonstrate the look of a larger piece). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Angie Xue always wanted to visit Japan and Korea. When she saw flights available from California, she immediately booked one. Xue’s first plan was to book a personal color analysis appointment in Seoul, which she learned about on social media. The analysis helps people find colors that suit them for clothing, makeup, and accessories based on their skin tones. Color consultants spend about 60 minutes to see what colors light up your face. Thanks to Tik Tok, color analysis is becoming popular from California to New York, with Gen Z travelers who make trips to Seoul to experience it. Color consultants recommend jewelry and suggest makeup. Difficult words: analysis (detailed examination), accessory (a hat, belt, scarf, and similar things), consultant (a person who gives you professional advice). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Angie Xue is American. But she always wants to go to Japan and Korea. She finds a cheap flight from California for 600 dollars. She books it quickly. Xue wants to have a personal color analysis in Seoul. She sees it on social media. It is interesting for her. The analysis helps people find good colors for their clothes, makeup, and accessories . It all depends on the color of the skin. In 60 minutes, an expert helps you find your personal color. You get tips on makeup and accessories. Many young people travel to Seoul now to get their color analysis. Difficult words: flight (traveling by plane), analysis (detailed examination), accessory (a hat, belt, scarf, and similar things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Travelling to New York City can be expensive, but a new venture has managed to cut the cost of accommodation dramatically. For less than 40 dollars a night, tourists on a tight budget can enjoy million dollar views of Manhattan from the back of a taxi cab! Entrepreneur Jonathan Powley recently started offering vans and New York taxi cabs as overnight rentals on Airbnb. Each of the vehicles has been converted to accommodate a large bed and a fan. There obviously is no room for a bathroom in a cab, but Powley has made a list of restaurants in the area that let his guests use theirs. The so-called “rolling rooms” have already attracted plenty of attention from tourists seeking a central location without a big-city price tag – you’re only one stop from Grand Central Station, and three stops from Times Square in less than 10 minutes. The business owner said that he thinks, ‘People that do it are just the type that want to try something different.’ Difficult words: venture (a business which involves risk), budget (the money you want/can spend on something), entrepreneur (a businessman who comes up with a new idea). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Travelling to New York City can be expensive, but one entrepreneur can cut your accommodation costs dramatically. His customers can sleep in the back of a taxi cab for only 40 dollars a night! The taxi is in the city centre – only three stops from Times Square and one stop from Grand Central Station. People who try it also have a great view of Manhattan. The so-called “rolling rooms” already attracted a lot of attention from tourists. There is, however, one little problem. There is no bathroom in the taxi, but the customers can use the bathroom of some restaurants. Difficult words: entrepreneur (businessman), accommodation (a place for somebody to sleep), attention (interest). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Hotels in New York are expensive. People want to visit New York, but they do not have enough money. One man knows this. He offers cheap accommodation . It costs only 40 dollars a night. You do not stay in a hotel. You stay in a taxi. There is a bed in the taxi. However, there is no bathroom. You must use a restaurant bathroom. People like this type of accommodation. The taxi is in the city centre. It is only three stops from Times Square, and only one stop from Grand Central Station. You also have a great view of Manhattan. Difficult words: offer (if you offer something, people can buy it from you), accommodation (a place where you can sleep), view (what you can see). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Wildfires have ravaged nine countries in the Mediterranean region, causing the death of at least 40 people, with Algeria being the worst affected. The northern mountainous region of Algeria reported 34 fatalities while neighboring Tunisia also battled wildfires. Italy experienced numerous wildfires in Sicily and Calabria during a severe heatwave, resulting in two deaths. Firefighters in Turkey, Croatia, Syria, Gran Canaria, and Portugal also fought against the spreading fires. Scientist Izidine Pinto emphasized that the increasing frequency and intensity of these wildfires are directly linked to the human- induced climate emergency. Difficult words: ravage (to cause severe damage), fatality (death), induce (to cause). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Wildfires swept through nine countries in the Mediterranean, which led to the loss of 40 lives, mostly in Algeria. Algeria’s authorities reported 34 deaths in the mountainous northern region, while Tunisia also faced wildfires. In Italy, during an extreme heatwave, Sicily and Calabria experienced many wildfires, which claimed two lives. Firefighters fought against blazes in Turkey, Croatia, Syria, Gran Canaria, and a natural park near Lisbon, Portugal. Scientist Izidine Pinto said that the increasing frequency and intensity of these wildfires were directly linked to the climate crisis which people caused. Difficult words: blaze (a big fire), frequency (how often something happens), intensity (how strong something is). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Wildfires are in nine Mediterranean countries. At least 40 people die. Algeria has the biggest problems. A region in the mountains is on fire. 34 people die there. Neighboring Tunisia also has wildfires. A heatwave hits Sicily and Calabria in Italy. There are many wildfires because of the hot weather. Firefighters in Turkey, Croatia, Syria, and Gran Canaria fight with fires. Another fire is in a natural park near Lisbon, Portugal. Scientists say that people make all these problems. The weather is changing. Fires happen more often. And they are bigger and more dangerous. Difficult words: wildfire (a fire in nature), region (a part of a country), heatwave (a period when the weather is very hot). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Have you ever wondered how astronauts go to the loo in space? Thankfully, British astronaut Tim Peake has explained. He shows that there is a tube which you pee in, and its fan keeps everything going down the pipe. You go number two the same way. Difficult words: number two (poo). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A British astronaut films videos in space. He recently showed us how astronauts make coffee, and now, how they use the toilet. Space toilets must have fans . You turn the fan on, you pee in a tube, and the pee goes down the tube . If you forget to turn on the fan, the pee flies around! Difficult words: fan (a thing which moves air), pee (to let out the yellowish “water” out of your body), tube (a thin, long thing with space in the middle). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A British astronaut is in space. He films videos. He shows people how to do things in space. For example, he shows people how to make coffee. He also shows people how to use the toilet. The space toilet is not like your normal toilet. It has a fan and you pee in a tube . The fan moves the air and the pee into the tube. Do not forget to turn on the fan! If you forget, the pee flies around you. Difficult words: fan (a things which moves air), pee (to let out the yellowish “water” out of your body), tube (a thin, long thing with space in the middle). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In northwest China, people rarely see snow leopards in the wild but an avid wildlife photographer found a way to take their pictures. By following footprints in the snow and finding excrement , he determined that snow leopards were in the area, and he hid an infrared camera in the rocks of the 4,600-metre-high Burhan Budai Mountains. The camera caught pictures of the endangered animal. The snow leopards are under state level protection in China, making these rare pictures very special. Difficult words: avid (enthusiastic), infrared (made up of light that we are unable to see), excrement (the scientific word for poop), endangered (in danger of being destroyed). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Snow leopards are hard to see in the wild but an enthusiast wildlife photographer found a way to film these animals in northwest China. The photographer followed footprints in the snow and then he hid his camera in nearby rocks. The special camera was hidden on the 4,600-metre-high mountains and it called the snow leopard’s attention. There are only a few of these animals in China and they are under state protection. The pictures of the leopard are very special. Difficult words: footprint (mark made by a foot), nearby (near). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In nature, it is very difficult to see a snow leopard. One photographer filmed a snow leopard in China. The photographer saw the leopard’s footprints in the snow. He put his camera on a rock. The special camera was 4,600 metres high in the mountains. The camera filmed the leopard. The camera was interesting for the leopard. There are not many snow leopards in China. They are under state protection. The pictures of the leopard are very special. Difficult words: difficult (not easy), footprint (a mark made by a foot). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Two tiny and adorable baby pygmy marmosets were born at Sydney’s Symbio Wildlife Park. They weighed just 15 grammes at birth (and were the size of human thumbs) but giving birth to them was, from the mother’s perspective, comparable to a human giving birth to a ten-year-old child. Their proud parents Gomez and IT were introduced to each other the previous year, when IT, the female, arrived at the zoo. Years of bachelorhood ended for Gomez and the two started a family. Apart from their baby monkeys being very cute, their birth is necessary for the ongoing survival of the endangered species . They are members of the world’s smallest monkey species, with adults weighing in at around the same weight as an average apple, just 100 grammes. They are facing extinction due to deforestation and illegal pet trade. Difficult words: tiny (very small), adorable (lovable, cute, sweet), comparable (similar), bachelorhood (living as a bachelor – unmarried/single man), endangered species (an animal kind which may die out soon), extinction (dying out), due to (because of), deforestation (destroying forests). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The smallest monkey in the world weighs only 100 grams. That is as much as an apple. The species is endangered because people are destroying the forests where this type of monkey lives. A zoo in Sydney is trying to help the species survive. Zoo keepers put together two monkeys to start a monkey family. A year later, two lovely monkeys were born. They weigh just 15 grams and are smaller than a human thumb! The monkeys are really cute . Check out their video! Difficult words: species (an animal kind/type), endangered (in danger of dying out), cute (beautiful). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is about monkeys. It is about the smallest monkeys in the world. The smallest monkeys are only 100 grams heavy. There aren’t many of these monkeys in the wild . They are in danger because people are destroying forests . A zoo in Sydney wants to help the monkeys. The zoo puts together two monkeys. It lets them have a family. Two baby monkeys are born. They are beautiful and they are very, very small. They are just 15 grams heavy. They are smaller than your thumb. Difficult words: in the wild (not in a zoo, free), destroy (to break), forest (a big group of trees). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Israel’s parliament recently approved new legislation that curtails some powers of the Supreme Court, despite widespread protests and concerns from the United States. The amendment removes the Supreme Court’s ability to void executive decisions deemed unreasonable, though they can still rule against the government using other legal grounds. Critics argue that this change could lead to corruption and weaken checks on government power. They fear that government officials may not scrutinize their policies thoroughly enough, potentially causing injustice in the long run. Many people in Israel fear that this is just the beginning of a larger assault on democracy, as the government had previously proposed an overhaul of the judiciary. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu plans to change the way judges are selected; however, it remains uncertain if there will be a consensus on further changes. Critics are concerned that Netanyahu may use the judicial changes to influence his ongoing corruption trial, but Netanyahu denies that. Difficult words: curtail (impose a restriction on), scrutinize (examine closely), overhaul (a thorough reorganization), consensus (a general agreement). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Israel’s parliament approved new laws which will reduce the power of the Supreme Court. Before this change, the court could cancel government decisions if it found them unreasonable . Now, that power is gone, but the court can still rule against the government using other laws. People worry that corruption might increase because government officials could more easily hire and fire people for the wrong reasons. Experts see Israel’s democracy, and so, the Supreme Court is important to protect people’s rights and the law. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu wants to make more changes, but it is unclear if everyone will agree. People are afraid he might use these changes to help himself in his corruption trial, but he denies this. Difficult words: unreasonable (not fair and sensible), corruption (when people in power do bad things), deny (to say that something is not true). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Israel, the parliament makes new laws. The Supreme Court has less power now. Many people do not like this. They protest. The US is worried, too. The court cannot stop government decisions anymore. Some people think that this will make the government more corrupt . They are also scared that the government will not be so fair. Israel’s democracy is not very strong. So, the Supreme Court is very important. It protects people’s rights and the law. The leader Benjamin Netanyahu wants more changes. But people are not sure about them.
